title: Path of the Dead
subtitle: Tonatiuh, bless the souls of the warriors. Let them break free from their cocoons. Let them return.

items.text: Family Ofrenda
The night is made hazy with the smoke of an uncountable number of candles.
The ofrenda holds food and drinks. Marigolds glow in vivid colors. Pictures and paintings of the dead smile down on the living.

items.speaker: Wealthy Businesswoman
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, it is my great honor to join you in celebrating All Souls' Day on this fabulous evening.

items.speaker: Wealthy Businesswoman
items.text: Ah, you must be Mr. Mack from the United States. How are you enjoying your stay in Mexico City? Just as I promised, is it not?

items.speaker: Guest
items.text: Mighty fine indeed! Thanks again for your invitation, ma'am. I have to say, I've been eager to meet you in person.

items.speaker: Guest
items.text: I think I'm falling in love with this city already.

items.speaker: Wealthy Businesswoman
items.text: Well, the party's only just begun. Many more truly unprecedented experiences await. Believe me.
An unexpected visitor appears at the entrance.

items.speaker: Wealthy Businesswoman
items.text: Well, look who it is. A pleasant surprise indeed.

items.speaker: Wealthy Businesswoman
items.text: I thought you weren't coming, Mr. Añil.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Good evening, Ms. Juárez.

items.speaker: Wealthy Businesswoman
items.text: I owe you my thanks for your beautiful restoration of the murals on my family's tomb. I do so hope you enjoy yourself tonight.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I'm sure I will. Thank you for your kind invitation, ma'am.
He walks toward the brilliantly decorated ofrenda, his grim-faced presence clashing with the joyful atmosphere.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: This was a mistake, for her and for me.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Ms. Ramona is nowhere to be seen. Perhaps she isn't coming? No, she'll show her face. She's sure to recognize the significance of that list.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And Ms. Butterfly must be hidden somewhere nearby. Taken her seat for the drama, no doubt.
The place falls silent. A deep, official voice speaks over the microphone.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Ahem, I would like to express my thanks to Mrs. Juárez for kindly hosting us tonight. Here in Mexico City, I have been able to witness and feel the beauty of your culture.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: The Day of the Dead celebration has shown me the extraordinary way in which the Mexican people remember, celebrate, and reunite with their departed loved ones, and I have truly been moved by it.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Now, please join me in raising a toast. To all those passed and to all who yet live.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Let the party begin!
Guests laugh and toast, raising their glasses in a show of respect to the diplomat.
Yet as the attendees sip their drinks and cheer, someone approaches and whispers to the diplomat. The glasses have not even lowered before the two of them step away from view.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: He seems on edge. Did something happen?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I should follow him.
But his motion is cut off by another arrival.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You didn't say you'd be here.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I couldn't help but worry about you, after I gave you that list.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Hah. You can't even protect yourself. Why are you worrying about anyone else?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Get outta here before the killer makes a move.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Place is crowded. No one's gonna bother to save you when they strike.
She shifts her eyes over to the diplomat as she speaks. He is standing in a quiet corner, speaking with someone who appears to be a younger aide.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: What? How could that be?

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Enough of your excuses! In any case, we mustn't let Mrs. Juárez get wind of this.
The diplomat scolds him, and they begin to argue. The aide shifts nervously and then shoots his hand into his pocket.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Oh, no!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: He's got a weapon. We gotta stop him.
The thought-to-be assailant falls to the ground. He lifts his hand from his pocket, revealing nothing more than festive candy likely taken from an ofrenda far too soon.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: What on earth is wrong with you? Think you could go around roughing up my men?

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Who are you, some local gangsters?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Sir, listen, you're in serious danger. He was gonna assassinate you.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: What nonsense are you spouting? He was just delivering a report.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: It's the painting I gave Mrs. Juárez. Apparently the color has faded in one spot. My assistant was only asking me to check it over.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: A painting from the Turquoise Serpent Club? Where is it? You need to give it to me, now.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: If you want to live, you need to stay away from that painting.
The diplomat's mood shifts. He seems frightened, certainly, but not of the painting she warns him about.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: You're from one of those xenophobic arcanist groups, aren't you? Mrs. Juárez warned me about people like you.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: What are you planning to do, huh? Kill me in front of all these people?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: No, no, sir. Listen to me. I'm trying to help you.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Help! Intruders! Hel—argh ...
His words stop. A painful rasp replaces them. He grabs his throat, struggling for air.
They have moved without noticing to the part of the courtyard where gifts are displayed.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: What on earth ...? Sir, are you all right?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Don't get too close. That arcane power could drown you along with him.

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: Argggh. Wh-Where am I? Is that a lake beneath the water?

items.speaker: Foreign Diplomat
items.text: H-Help ...
The diplomat's voice falls into a rasp, then silence. He crumples into a heap on the ground.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: This is just like ...

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Like what happened at the auction.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The killer can't be far. Must still be hiding somewhere near the ofrenda.
Ramona hears a rustle in the grass behind her. She turns with just enough time to spy a figure darting away.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: There! Get 'em!
The city street is crowded with people celebrating. The raucous mood and shifting mass of people obscure sight in every direction.
They have lost sight of their culprit.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: *pant* Damn it.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: *pant* We lost them.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: This is a wealthy area. The mansions on this street must have guards at their entrances. We can ask them if they saw anyone suspicious.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: No time for that.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The paintings are the key to the killer's m.o., but what else am I missing?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The diplomat already had the painting for a while before the party.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That journalist must have given it to him a few days ago.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: So, why'd the killer wait so long, and why strike in front of so many people? Why do it on the night of one of our biggest festivals?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That's gotta be it. It's all about the timing.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Timing, you say? So, it has something to do with All Souls' Day.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That's right, the second night of Day of the Dead. The night we welcome back and reunite with the faithful departed.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Death is just a part of the cycle of life, right? I'd bet the killer thinks so too.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: And they chose tonight because they're trying to lead the spirits of the victims somewhere? Someplace they aren't meant to be?
She looks down. Countless marigold petals spread out beneath her feet, forming a path to guide the dead. It stretches far into the distance.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Huh. That may be the answer. See, someone's laid a trail of marigolds out the back door.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The vivid glow of marigolds is what's said to guide spirits back to the land of the living.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: They want us to follow this path, huh? Fine, then let's go.
A quiet, stately building marks the end of the marigold trail.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You're kidding.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Of all the places ...
